name: AudioMixer
signature: public sealed class AudioMixer : Asset, ISerializationCallbackReceiver

docs.summary: An asset describing how audio is routed and mixed: a tree of [`AudioMixerGroup`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioMixerGroup) buses that sources feed into, so volumes can be set per category rather than per source.
Every group in the mixer. The first is the root that all others eventually feed into.
The root group everything in this mixer feeds into.
True while any bus in this mixer is soloed, which is what silences the rest.
Clears every solo in the mixer.
Pushes every bus's level across again. Needed after anything that changes what a bus should be doing without touching its own fields, which is what a solo somewhere else is.

members.name: SetParent
members.signature: public bool SetParent(AudioMixerGroup group, AudioMixerGroup parent)

docs.summary: Re-routes `group` to feed `parent`, or the output when that is null. Refuses anything that would make a bus feed itself, directly or through its own children.
Finds a group by name, or null. Names are compared exactly.

members.name: AddGroup
members.signature: public AudioMixerGroup AddGroup(string groupName, AudioMixerGroup parent = null)

docs.summary: Adds a group feeding into `parent`, or into the root when that is null.
Removes a group, re-pointing anything that fed into it at its own parent. Sources still routed to it fall back to the master output.
docs.remarks: The group's native objects are released, but the object itself is left alive. It is a sub-asset, so anything holding an [`OutputGroup`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~OutputGroup) reference to it still has one, and destroying it here would leave those sources pointing at a destroyed object rather than at nothing. Its disappearance from the asset database is the reimport's business, which is how the rest of the sub-asset machinery works.

docs.summary: Drops every native object this mixer built. They are rebuilt on next use.
Every recorded mix this mixer can be moved to.
The snapshot this mixer was last moved to, or is on its way to.
True while a transition between snapshots is still running.
Finds a snapshot by name, or null. Names are compared exactly.
Records the mixer as it is now under a new name, and returns the snapshot.
Puts the mixer into a recorded mix at once, with nothing to ease.

members.name: TransitionTo
members.signature: public void TransitionTo(AudioMixerSnapshot snapshot, float seconds)

docs.summary: Moves the mixer to a recorded mix over `seconds`, which is what a change of scene, a pause menu or going underwater actually is.
docs.remarks: Starts from wherever the mixer is now rather than from whatever it was last told to be, so a transition interrupted by another one carries on from what you can currently hear instead of jumping back. Flags cross at the half way mark, since a mute has no midpoint to ease through.

members.name: TransitionTo
members.signature: public void TransitionTo(string name, float seconds)

docs.summary: Moves to the snapshot with this name, if there is one.
Advances every running snapshot transition. Driven by the audio update, and cheap to call when nothing is transitioning, which is almost always.
docs.remarks: Measured against the wall clock rather than the game's, because a mix change belongs to what the player is hearing: a pause menu that fades the music over a third of a second has to take a third of a second even though the thing it is fading for has stopped time.

docs.summary: Groups arrive knowing their parent's index but not which mixer they belong to.
